mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 0.75% over the prior month compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as monetary policy accommodates economic weakness.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.1% over the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 0.75% and rises by more than 0.1 percentage points in one month, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 0.75% and rising > 0.1pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1700 and retail sales (RSAFS) below 670,000,000,000, indicates weakening consumer demand that reduces corporate earnings expectations, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when HOUST < 1700 and RSAFS < 670000.0 in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-unemployment regime (UNRATE < 3.5%), a rising employment level (PAYEMS) above 150,000,000 signals labor market tightness that fuels inflationary expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as central bank policy tightens.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 3.5% and PAYEMS rises > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 and falling for two consecutive months indicates supply chain contraction that reduces corporate output, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0 and declining > 0.5% in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 290.0 and rising for three consecutive months signals strong inflation-adjusted demand, supporting corporate earnings growth and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 290.0 and rising for three months.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 290.0 and accelerates by more than 0.5 percentage points per month, it triggers aggressive monetary tightening that increases equity discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 290.0 and accelerating > 0.5pp in 1 month.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-employment regime (PAYEMS > 150,000), a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.5% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth slows.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE > 3.5%.
